Like many, I was a bit anxious about booking an appointment, especially with everything you hear in the media about the pressures on the NHS. I really didn’t want to add to the strain.

However, I was pleasantly surprised by how easy and efficient the whole experience was. I was able to get a same-day appointment when I urgently needed it. After a short wait, I was seen by the doctor, who was professional, efficient, and quickly prescribed the antibiotics I needed.

To top it off, the pharmacy was right next door, so I was able to collect my medication immediately—such a relief!

Fantastic service all round. difficult to get to see a doctor or even a telephone appointment. If calling the reception team one is directed to an online triage form which has the message: "We have paused access to contact us online as we have reached capacity for the day." If one subsequently calls the reception team they tell you to try again at 8am the following day. I am not feeling well enough to get up and go online at 8am but apparently there is no alternative. The online triage form was "paused" last Thursday, Friday and is again paused today Monday. It seems totally nonsensical to me that the system discriminates against the unwell who are supposed to be the focus of this service in unless I misunderstand? Why indeed can the online triage form not be paused but instead roll over to the next day or beyond if need be?
